task: Bug: `tenacity.after_log` crashes with `TypeError` when `retry_state.seconds_since_start` is `None` (it is `None` when the outcome timestamp has not been set). The log message should still be emitted, showing "?" in place of the elapsed seconds.
why:
The deciding criterion was fidelity to the existing test conventions. c3 reads `seconds_since_start` into a local once, then puts its test in the existing `TestAfterLogFormat` class with the `test_03_` naming and reuses `self.previous_attempt_number`/`self.log_level`.
The runner-up, c2, does the same but evaluates the property twice and has a needless f-string with no placeholders (`f"after ?(s), "`).
c1 is equivalent but adds a whole new test class when the existing one fits.
c4 imports `RetryCallState` and builds it by hand with a `# type: ignore` instead of using the existing `make_retry_state` helper.
